title: Fire didn’t fall because no one cared.
paragraphs: Fire didn’t fall because no one cared.
It fell because almost no one was left to pray.
Because Abraham stood between heaven and a burning city… and begged God to hold back judgment.
But here’s the question that won’t leave me:
Who is standing in the gap for your generation right now?

Who is pleading for your family?
Your friends?
That one person you silently gave up on?
Or have we become so used to sin… that we’ve stopped interceding?
Abraham saw the wickedness of Sodom.

He didn’t deny it.
He didn’t soften it.
He didn’t rebrand it.

Sin was loud.
Corruption was public.
Darkness was deep.

“Will you sweep away the righteous with the wicked?”
“What if there are fifty… forty… thirty… twenty… ten?”
But because Abraham had a heart that refused to stop believing God could still show it.
He negotiated with heaven… not to excuse sin—but to give sinners time.
Because this is where conviction hits.
Some of us don’t pray like Abraham.

We cancel them.
Judge them.
Secretly enjoy their downfall.
But heaven might call it indifference.
Because it’s easier to expose darkness than to intercede for it.
Easier to preach judgment than to carry someone in prayer.
Easier to feel righteous… than to be broken.

“Behold, I have undertaken to speak to the Lord, I who am but dust and ashes.”
(Genesis 18:27)
Here’s the lesson that pierced me:
A heart close to God doesn’t become harsher toward sinners…
It becomes heavier with burden for them.
You start to feel what God feels.
And God does not delight in destruction.

“The Lord is… not wishing that any should perish, but that all should reach repentance.”
(2 Peter 3:9)
But His heart is still calling sinners home.
Because Abraham could only ask for mercy.
Jesus stepped into our broken world.

“For our sake He made Him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.”
(2 Corinthians 5:21)
We are the ones who deserved the fire.
And Jesus didn’t just pray for us.
So that mercy could fall where fire should have.

Not behavior management.
Not self-improvement.
Not religious performance.
You were not spared because you were good.
You were spared because Jesus was crushed in your place.
“But He was pierced for our transgressions; He was crushed for our iniquities… and by His wounds we are healed.”
Why are you refusing to stand for others?
If mercy found you in your worst moment…
Why have you stopped praying for theirs?
Why are you so quick to close the book on someone else?
Intercession is not optional for a believer.
Evidence that your heart has been touched by God.
Because saved people don’t just avoid sin…
Maybe that person you’re tired of…
God is not done with them.
Maybe that situation you think is too far gone…
Heaven is still listening for someone to ask.
What if the miracle is waiting on your prayer?
What if mercy is waiting on your voice?
You cannot stand for others… while running from God yourself.
Or are you hiding behind someone else’s sin to avoid your own?
Not to agree and move on.

Lay down the pride.
Lay down the secret sin.
Lay down the judgment in your heart.
And receive what Jesus already paid for.
Because as long as there is breath…
If this hit your heart, don’t ignore it.
